newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Petronas says 38bln Samurai bond fully subscribed.
newsitem.headline: Petronas says 38bln Samurai bond fully subscribed.

text.p: Malaysian state oil firm Petronas said on Thursday that its issue of Samurai bonds worth 38 billion yen on the Japanese capital markets had been fully subscribed.
Petronas had undertaken the bond issue to repay earlier loans from Japan and company president Hassan Marican told a news conference that the weakening of the yen will further ease Petronas' burden.
"We were borrowing yen to repay yen and I think our loans are better restructed now," Hassan said.
He said Petronas only incurred half the interest rate -- two percent -- for the bond issue, compared to four percent under its earlier loans.
"The bonds have been fully subscribed and the weakening of the yen has helped our borrowings further," Hassan said.
The bonds, lead managed by Daiwa Securities Co Ltd were launched on February 28 in three tranches, two of 11 billion yen and one of 16 billion yen, Petronas said last week.
The maturity period for the three tranches are six, 10 and 16.5 years, respectively.
The coupon rates of each tranche are 2.15 percent, 2.9 percent and 3.4 percent.
